## Standards

1. **Hard violation — `README.md:129–131`.** The new documentation reproduces exact schema/runtime-owned details: “closed JSON object with exactly `version`…”, complete allowed tool/prerequisite vocabularies, proposal field optionality, and cardinality rules. `CLAUDE.md:12` assigns field names, types, optionality, and semantics to schemas; `CLAUDE.md:36` requires duplicated rules to remain at their deepest owner. Keep README caller-facing usage and reference the authoritative schema rather than duplicating its complete vocabulary.

2. **Judgement call — possible Duplicated Code, `test/reviewer-role.test.ts:116,143,160,185,199`.** Multiple tests repeat the same activation sequence:

   > `handlers.get("input")({text:"review"}); handlers.get("before_agent_start")({prompt:"review",systemPrompt:"system"});`

   Extracting a small expansion/activation helper would reduce repetition and prevent setup details drifting between tests.

No other documented-standard breach or baseline smell was established. No probe changes or scratch artifacts were added to the reviewed clone.

## Spec

1. **[P1] Compiled child prompts do not bind the exact canonical Skill snapshot.**  
   Spec: “**A changed canonical snapshot must change extracted prompt evidence without changing source constants.**”

   `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:411-429` includes task/range provenance and selected Skill excerpts, but no canonical-Skill identity in either prompt. Although `canonicalSkillSha256` is stored separately at line 463, changing any unextracted Skill content leaves both provider-facing prompt bytes and hashes unchanged. This fails the required snapshot-to-prompt binding. The Skill digest should be part of the common provenance block.

2. **[P2] The recompilation check does not reproduce the construction recipe.**  
   Spec: “**verify recompilation identity before acceptance**” and mechanically reject “**any output not reproduced exactly by the selected construction recipe**.”

   At `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts:423-436`, each prompt string is constructed once and placed in `promptInputs`; both “compilations” then merely hash that same already-built string. Material rendering, Skill-section extraction, provenance assembly, and axis composition are never replayed. Consequently, the check cannot detect nondeterminism or divergence in the actual construction recipe—only a stateful hashing hook. Recompile twice from the frozen construction inputs instead.

No additional scope creep was established. No reviewed-clone files or probe changes were created; the diff tool’s capture was scratch outside the clone.

**Summary:** Standards: 2 findings; worst is the hard README/schema-runtime ownership violation. Spec: 2 findings; worst is the P1 failure to bind compiled prompts to the exact canonical Skill snapshot.
